title: Paint Sheens Explained: Which Finish to Use in Each Room
description: Use flat on ceilings, matte or eggshell on most walls, satin in kitchens, baths and kids' rooms, and semi-gloss on trim, doors and cabinets. Here's how each paint sheen looks, cleans and holds up.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: use flat on ceilings, matte or eggshell on most walls, satin in kitchens, bathrooms, hallways and kids' rooms, and semi-gloss on trim, doors and cabinets. The shinier the finish, the easier it is to clean, and the more it shows flaws in the surface.

The Paint Sheens, From Dullest to Shiniest

Flat

No shine. Hides patches, seams and uneven drywall better than any other sheen. It's the hardest to scrub, so it's best for ceilings and low-traffic rooms. See ceiling painting.

Matte

Almost no shine, but more washable than traditional flat. A popular choice for living rooms, dining rooms and bedrooms when you want a soft look. See bedroom painting and dining room painting.

Eggshell

A low, soft glow. It's the most common wall finish because it balances hiding flaws with being wipeable. Good for most living areas and hallways.

Satin

A noticeable sheen that stands up to scrubbing and moisture. Good for kitchens, bathrooms, laundry rooms and kids' rooms. It shows wall imperfections more than eggshell does, so prep matters.

Semi-gloss

Shiny, hard and very washable. The standard for trim, baseboards, doors and many cabinets. It highlights detail in millwork and makes walls with any flaws look worse, so it's rarely used on whole walls.

Gloss

The highest shine and the hardest surface. Used for front doors, furniture and accents. Every flaw shows, so it needs the best prep of any sheen.

How to Choose

  • The more traffic and moisture, the more sheen. Bathrooms and kids' rooms need washability.

  • The more flaws, the less sheen. Older walls with patches look best in flat, matte or eggshell.

  • Contrast walls and trim. A lower-sheen wall next to semi-gloss trim makes the trim stand out cleanly.

  • Same color, different sheen looks different. A higher sheen makes the same color look slightly darker and richer.

  • Sheen names vary by brand. One brand's eggshell may be close to another's satin. Compare actual samples.

What About Exterior Sheens?

For most Texas exteriors, a low-sheen or satin finish on the body of the house and semi-gloss on trim and doors is a good balance. Low sheen sheds dirt and rain better than flat while still hiding surface texture.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the most popular paint sheen for walls?

Eggshell, followed by matte. Both hide minor flaws and can be wiped clean.

Is satin or semi-gloss better for bathrooms?

Satin for bathroom walls; semi-gloss for bathroom trim and doors. Both resist moisture better than flat or matte.

What sheen should trim be?

Semi-gloss is the standard. Satin is a softer option if you prefer less shine.
